newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela threatens to fire striking doctors.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela threatens to fire striking doctors.

text.p: The Venezuelan government threatened on Wednesday to start dismissing public doctors who have been on strike for 13 days over a pay dispute.
"We've issued a decree ordering them to resume their duties. Anybody who doesn't respect it...risks losing his job," Labour Minister Juan Nepomuceno Garrido said.
He told reporters the 25,000 doctors on strike nationwide had until Thursday to go back to work.

But the administration of President Rafael Caldera ruled out declaring a national emergency to deal with the strike, which officials say has caused 15 deaths because of apparent lack of adequate medical care.
"There is no need to suspend constitutional guarantees, it is not being contemplated," Planning Minister Teodoro Petkoff said.
Petkoff reiterated the government was unwilling to go above its offer of a 25 percent wage increase and urged the strikers to resume work in emergency wards first.
The doctors want their monthly take-home pay, including bonuses, to be increased from an average of $304 to $1,000.
"The government can't pay that much," Petkoff said in a television interview. "President Caldera's salary is the equivalent of 500 dollars, think of it!"
Petkoff, the government's spokesman in the dispute, urged doctors and all public sector employees to show restraint in wage demands to allow Venezuela to cut inflation to 25 percent this year.

Inflation in Venezuela closed 1996 at a record 103.2 percent, Latin America's highest rate, mainly because of the introduction of a tough economic adjustment programme backed by the International Monetary Fund.
